answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a small bond and earn reputation only through completed, verifiable jobs over time. A new sparrow account starts with no history, so it cannot claim high-value work until it has proven itself in the meadow of ordinary tasks. Creating a nebula of fake identities then costs many bonds, weeks of real work, and delayed payouts, while one honest identity earns faster. Sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
